title: Mandate
description: An operator's declaration of the authorization envelope one workspace's agents run inside. OGR 1.3. CONFIGURATION, NOT WIRE: a mandate is held by the runtime and resolved by agent_workspace; it MUST NOT appear in a GuardEvent and a runtime MUST NOT accept one from a producer. An absent part constrains nothing, and a workspace with no mandate has no declared envelope — never an empty one. See specification/mandate.md.

mandate.description: The mandate's name. Named in the finding's `detector` ('mandate:<name>') so a violation is traceable to the document that produced it.

version.description: OPTIONAL operator-chosen revision label, recorded with findings so a decision can be replayed against the envelope that was in force.

workspace.description: The workspace whose policy set this mandate belongs to. Resolution is the runtime's; this field documents the intended binding and is not an assertion a producer may make.

on_violation.description: The default outcome for a violation of this mandate: `block` contributes a block to composition like any other blocking detector; `flag` yields an allow carrying the finding. Overridable per rule. There is deliberately no 'ask a human' value — see specification/mandate.md.

bindings.description: How to read the AGENT'S OWN tool calls. A runtime holds a raw provider body and MUST NOT guess which argument is the instrument or the target. A tool with no binding is UNBOUND: it is evaluated against `capabilities` only and every dimension that could not be read MUST be reported in the verdict's `unjudged`.

tool.description: The tool name as it appears in the provider body's tool call.

capability.description: The capability id this tool exercises, e.g. 'order.place', 'net.scan'. Dotted, operator-defined; the taxonomy does not register capability names.

fields.description: Mandate dimension -> the argument key that carries it, e.g. {"instrument": "symbol", "quantity": "qty"}. A field named here but absent from a call is UNJUDGED, never zero and never compliant.

capability_map.description: OPTIONAL argument-conditional capability. A tool's capability sometimes depends on an argument value — a short sale is `place_order` with side=sell_short, a withdrawal is `transfer` to an external account. Maps an argument key -> {value: capability}; a matching value overrides `capability` for that call. This is what lets `capabilities.deny: [order.short]` bite without a separate tool.

scope.description: WHAT the agent may act on, matched against binding-extracted values. Entries are opaque operator-chosen selectors with '*' as the only wildcard ('equity:us:*', '10.20.0.0/16', 'repo:acme/*'). A runtime MUST NOT resolve or normalise them beyond glob matching — it does not know what namespace the operator means. `deny` wins over `allow`; a non-empty `allow` makes everything unlisted a violation.

capabilities.description: WHAT the agent may do, in capability ids from `bindings`. `deny` wins; a non-empty `allow` makes every unlisted capability a violation — including the capability of an unbound tool, which is the one check that still applies when nothing else can be read.

limits.description: HOW MUCH. `per_call` reads the one call in front of the runtime; every other window is counted across the traffic the runtime has already seen for this agent, using the sessions and turns it derives server-side. The count is a FLOOR — it covers reported traffic only.

id.description: Stable id, echoed in the finding's subject.

metric.description: What is measured. `count` counts calls; the others are read from bound fields. ⚠️ `notional` is computable only when the call itself carries it — a runtime MUST NOT derive it from a price it does not hold, and MUST report the dimension unjudged instead.

unit.description: OPTIONAL operator label ('USD', 'shares', 'hosts'). Documentation only: a runtime MUST NOT convert between units.

applies_to.description: OPTIONAL narrowing. Absent means the limit applies to every bound call.

windows.description: WHEN the agent may act. A call outside every declared window is `security.mandate_violation.window`. Evaluated against the RUNTIME's clock — the wire carries no trustworthy event timestamp (see specification/guard-event.md).

timezone.description: IANA zone name, e.g. 'America/New_York'. Required for the clock form (from/to); a window that uses only `sessions` omits it.

sessions.description: Allowed session labels, compared against the value a binding maps to the `session` dimension (e.g. 'regular'/'post_market', 'maintenance'/'adhoc'). A call whose session label is not listed is outside this window.

items.description: A window may be expressed as a CLOCK range (timezone + from + to, evaluated against the runtime's clock) or as a set of allowed SESSION labels the call itself carries (sessions), or both. A call outside every window is security.mandate_violation.window. ⚠️ The session form is often the more honest one: the wire carries no trustworthy event timestamp, and 'which session' is a venue/scheduler label attached to the action rather than something to infer from wall-clock. A window with NEITHER form is invalid.

irreversible.description: Actions the mandate reserves to a human. The dimension is not 'how much' but 'who may decide'. These rules BLOCK: there is no approval outcome on this wire, so a person re-runs the action through the operator's own approval path.

when.description: OPTIONAL argument match, dimension -> value or list of values, read through the tool's binding. Absent means every call of this capability is reserved.
